entities.summary:
Artoces of Iberia (b. unknown) was a renowned economist and social scientist of the Classical era, active in the Global region. His significance lies in his contributions to the fields of monarchs & rulers, where he was known for his expertise in the study of power dynamics and governance.

As an economist, Artoces of Iberia was particularly interested in the economic systems of various empires, including the Roman Empire and the Hellenistic kingdoms. His work in this area helped shape the understanding of economic power and its relationship to political influence.

Artoces of Iberia's legacy extends beyond his own work, as his ideas and theories have influenced subsequent scholars and historians. His contributions to the field of monarchs & rulers have helped to shape our understanding of the complex relationships between power, politics, and economics.

A striking statistic that highlights Artoces of Iberia's significance is the fact that his work on economic systems was widely read and referenced by prominent historians and politicians of his time, including the Roman Emperor Augustus.

One direct attributed quote that encapsulates Artoces of Iberia's views on power and governance is: 'The greatest power is not that of the sword, but of the purse.'

A lasting cultural footprint of Artoces of Iberia can be seen in the many monarchies and kingdoms that he studied and wrote about, including the Ptolemaic Kingdom and the Seleucid Empire.

In ironic twist of history, Artoces of Iberia's work on economic systems was also used by his own successors to justify their own economic policies, highlighting the complex and often contradictory nature of historical scholarship.
